glossary.Clotting factors: Blood proteins that act in sequence to form a clot.
glossary.Factor VIII: A clotting factor of the intrinsic pathway; missing in haemophilia A.
glossary.Factor IX: A clotting factor of the intrinsic pathway; missing in haemophilia B. Also called Christmas factor.
glossary.Inherited bleeding disorder: A bleeding tendency passed on in the genes.
glossary.Muscular haematoma: A collection of blood within a muscle.
glossary.Easy bruising: Bruises appearing after minor or no injury.
glossary.Post-surgical bleeding: Bleeding that continues or restarts after an operation.
glossary.Deep bleeding: Bleeding into joints and muscles rather than the skin surface.
glossary.Joint damage: Wear and destruction of cartilage and bone from repeated bleeds.
glossary.Head injury: Any blow to the head; in haemophilia assume a bleed inside the skull.
glossary.ICH: Intracranial haemorrhage: bleeding inside the skull.
glossary.Symptomatic carrier: A female carrier who still bleeds, for example because she has only one X chromosome.
glossary.Platelet count: The number of platelets in the blood, normal in haemophilia.
glossary.Factor replacement: Giving the missing clotting factor into a vein.
glossary.Adjunct: A treatment added on to the main one.
glossary.Endothelial: Relating to the cells lining blood vessels.
glossary.Recombinant: Made in the lab using genetically engineered cells rather than from donated blood.
glossary.Prophylactic: Given to prevent a problem rather than treat it.
glossary.Joint protection: Rest, splinting and physiotherapy to stop a bleeding joint being damaged.
glossary.Coagulation cascade: The chain of clotting factors, each activating the next, ending in a fibrin clot.
glossary.Clot: A solid plug of platelets and fibrin that stops bleeding.
glossary.Platelet disorders: Conditions with too few or poorly working platelets, causing skin and mucosal bleeding.
glossary.Mucosal: Relating to the moist linings of the mouth, nose, gut and genital tract.
glossary.Mutation: A change in a gene's DNA.
glossary.Assay: A lab test measuring the amount or activity of a substance.
glossary.Gold standard: The most accurate test available for confirming a diagnosis.
glossary.Stabilises: Protects from breakdown; vWF carries factor VIII and stops it being cleared.
